analysis: Examined two base_text excerpts (lines 10757-12403) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. The patch excerpt shows the only visible changes are prompt_contract_id value replacements (6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3... on the head side) in the model-level field and the per-case plan.prompt_contract_id fields, plus the changed ranges listed for chain-hash lines (for example 10823-10830, 11716-11727). These are public synthetic test vectors for prompt-contract and cache-parity ("Public synthetic cache-parity input"). They contain no secrets, keys, tokens, or real consumer content. The base excerpts show the older contract ID a9e96abf... in some plan blocks, and the patch excerpt is truncated and the range map incomplete, so I cannot confirm the head-side values at those lines. The change is a fixture regeneration, not runtime code. Relevant threat context is T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and timing oracle). A changed prompt_contract_id and chain hashes would alter cache-key derivation, which scopes cache sharing. The fixtures are test data only. No authorization, attestation (TB-011, A-016), encryption, billing, or availability behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. Remaining integration questions: whether the matching Swift/Go code that computes prompt_contract_id and chain hashes changed in the same PR, and whether any change there weakens cache-scope isolation. Those files are not in this batch, so I could not review them. Because the head-side values and the corresponding implementation are unseen, no finding is supported.
